rounds:
Round 4 is the verdict recorded here: PASS, no blocker or major, no findings. Rounds 1-3 each failed on at least one major.

Round 1: 1 major on ui.chat.composer.steer_hint, whose « موجودہ باری » lacked the object marker « کو » and so read as unidiomatic Urdu; a minor on placeholder.waiting_both for naming the modes without saying what Enter and Esc do.

Round 2: 2 majors on ui.settings.shortcuts.row_help.send_steer and row_help.send_queue, whose « کو بدل دیتا ہے » said the shortcut changes the « مصروف ہونے پر ترسیل » setting rather than overriding it for this one message.

Round 3: 1 major on ui.chat.composer.placeholder.waiting_both, an ungrammatical fragment that did not say Enter first queues the message and then steers; a minor on ui.settings.shortcuts.row_help.send_steer, where « مرحلہ روک دیتا ہے » says the step stops rather than that it is interrupted, overstating the outcome against the shipped wording. The same overstatement was recorded as a finding on the backend twin, wire.settings.keymap.send_steer.help, in the same round.

Round 4 did NOT repeat that row_help.send_steer minor, and the wording on disk is unchanged from round 3: the retained record is round 4's verdict on these bytes, not a claim that every earlier minor was rewritten. The same is true of the canonical pass's one ur minor, on ui.chat.canonical.send_failure.delivery_unsupported (the imperative « ہدایت دیں » used as a mode name, where the corpus ships the noun « ہدایت »), which is recorded with its shipped value and disposition in the superseded receipt 2405ebc40b47-fold-ur.json and was not repeated in round 4; that value is also unchanged on disk.

ui.chat.canonical's own pass ran earlier: PASS with that single minor, and the fold2 rounds that followed did not reopen it.
